text: A dust storm swallowed the entire planet. The sky went dark.
A little rover called Opportunity had explored Mars for almost fifteen years. It lived on sunlight. And the sunlight was gone.
Its final signals, in simple words, said: my battery is low... and it's getting dark.
On Mars, a storm doesn't wait for you to be ready.
We are Bongo Aphelion, five builders from Bangladesh. And we asked one question: what if a child could get the crew ready... before the storm?
Children learn space as a list of facts. Mars is red. Astronauts need oxygen. But a real mission isn't a fact. It's a choice.
One battery. More air for the crew... or keep the science running?
Water to drink... or water to shield them from the Sun?
Every choice costs something. And almost no child ever gets to make one.
Right now, NASA is preparing to send people back to the Moon... and then on to Mars.
The people who will plan those missions are seven, eight, nine years old today. They'll need more than facts. They'll need judgment. And they can start practicing... now.
So we built Mission Control Jr. A free 3D game in any web browser. Nine missions, on Mars and the Moon. Built on real NASA science.
Then... you decide. Full light for the salad, or save the battery for tonight? There's no free answer.
Build a shelter from a real solar storm. Grow a birthday salad for a crewmate. Fix the water recycler while help from Earth is minutes away. Chase sunlight on the Moon.

Every mission stands on real NASA data: Opportunity's power in that 2018 storm, Curiosity's radiation readings, the HiRISE map of Jezero, lettuce grown on the Space Station. And the game shows kids where every number comes from.
When it's over, the report shows what worked, what didn't, and why. Then it asks: want to try a different plan? Here, failing isn't the end. It's the lesson.
Our goal isn't a high score. It's a child who can explain why their crew survived.
Next: real classrooms, live space-weather data, and more languages. We're looking for teachers, schools and mentors to take this journey with us.
Opportunity couldn't prepare for its storm.
The next generation can.
Mission Control Jr. Small decisions. Giant missions.
